occurrences.opportunityName: Help and Deliver Your Care at Paws United Charity Dog Adoption Centre
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Paws United Charity (PUC) is a non-profit, all-volunteer rescue organization established and registered in Hong Kong (ORG00102).

 

A group of animal-loving volunteers who are passionate about animal rescue and have worked together across various rescue projects in Hong Kong. After many years of hard work and dedication, they finally have a ‘home’ to call their own.



Volunteer roles:

1. Taking care and socializing with puppies

2. Cleansing

3. Assisting visitors by introducing Paws United Charity and the puppies to them



This will serve PUC’s core mission to continue to improve the lives of animals in our community by promoting responsible pet ownership, humane treatment of animals, and choosing adoption instead of purchase. 



Important Note: Please be aware that some dogs, particularly puppies, are very energetic and at times, boisterous. Volunteers should be comfortable handling dogs with this level of energy and enthusiasm, and we recommend wearing appropriate clothing (as detailed below) to minimise nips or scratches. 



Remarks:


	
Only successfully registered volunteers for this activity are allowed to join this activity. Please DO NOT bring any unregistered volunteers, your kids, or pets to volunteer.

	
Clothing: 
	

		
Wear something comfortable and things you don’t mind getting dirty in.

		
DO NOT wear clothes that are too loose or overly-exposed

		
NO swimwear, swim trunks, sandals, or slippers. 

	

	

	
Meals:
	

		
Please have your meal before coming as there is no meal break. We understand that the duty may be energy-consuming, but you are welcome to bring snacks/bread or small bites for a short snack break in centre.

occurrences.opportunityName: Help at animal shelter in Yuen Long (Youth Welcome)
occurrences.organizationServedName: Maison De Charlotte Pour Des Chats Et Des Chiens Sarl Limited (MCCC) 沙律貓狗之家
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Maison De Charlotte Pour Des Chats Et Des Chiens Sarl Limited (MCCC) is a small non-profit organization founded in 1997 and takes in about 200 animals. With no funding and limited manpower and resources, MCCC has been working hard for many years to provide a warm home to the countless rescued cats and dogs and let those waiting to be adopted live happily and have enough space for running and jumping. The founder’s mission is to "influence life with life" and fight for the right to survive for abandoned animals and provide them with the most appropriate medical treatment. They never make a hasty decision to end the life of an animal, nor delay or stingy medical expenses. They hope to disseminate information about respect for life, love for animals, "adopt, don’t abandon" and so on.

Volunteer roles:





	
Wash the water pockets for dogs and refill water

	
Clean up the dog's poo

	
Clean up areas where the dogs sleep, including blankets and towels

	
Assist in feeding the dogs, preparing meals, cleaning and washing dishes afterward

	
Have great fun with the dogs! 





Remarks:



	
Volunteers must be 16 years old or over. Parental consent is needed for volunteers age 16-17 years old. Please send an email to hohk@handsonhongkong.org with your parental consent to confirm your slots. 

	
Please note that this is an outdoor animal shelter without air-conditioners.







	
Volunteers are suggested to bring: 

	

		
At least 1-liter water & food 

		
​Sunscreen

		
Towels and an extra set of clothing for changing in case you get dirty.

		
A pair of slippers/rainboots for cleaning the kennel

Description:



LeadOn Hong Kong is a volunteer leadership program in Hong Kong led by young people roughly aged 18–35, run by the NGO HandsOn Hong Kong in partnership with HKEX Foundation. It is a structured leadership and community engagement program that guides and trains young people/adults to build the skills to design and lead creative community projects. serving local social needs.

 



Positioned as a bridge between young talent and the workforce, focusing on soft skills like communication, adaptability, and collaboration in a social-impact context. 

 



We are recruiting volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at board game-based service sessions for elderly people/young children at our partner NGO centres. These sessions use the power of play to create fun, structured opportunities for social interaction, cognitive stimulation, and skills-building in areas such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. These innovative board game workshops support social connection and cognitive engagement among elderly people and language development, creativity and confidence in children.





Children's Sessions (conduct in English through storytelling and board games):

Nov: 6, 7, 13, 14, 20, 21, 22, 27, 28

Dec: 4, 5, 11



Elderly Sessions:

Nov: 11, 17

Dec: 8, 9



Volunteer Roles:




	
Assist the Volunteer Leader and NGO staff in setting up the space, preparing game materials, and ensure all components are ready for use.

	
Join small groups to play board games with elderly participants/ children, modelling turn-taking, active listening, and inclusive participation.

	
​Support the Volunteer Leader in explaining simple game rules, encouraging quieter participants, and gently managing basic group dynamics during play.

	
Assist with smooth logistics such as registration, time-keeping, transition between games, and packing up at the end of the session.

	
​Participate in a briefing session and debriefing reflection to share what you observed about participants’ engagement and interactions.

	 





Remarks:




	
In this role, you will not be responsible for designing the program; you will be supporting trained Volunteer Leaders who have completed LeadOn’s Board Game Mastery and facilitation training to run impactful, participant-centred sessions.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

The founder’s mission is to "influence life with life" and fight for the right to survive for abandoned animals and provide them with the most appropriate medical treatment. occurrences.organizationServedName: Youth With A Mission Tuen Mun Hong Kong
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description:  Job losses and financial hardships have led to a notable rise in families seeking assistance from charities for essential food needs. YWAM Tuen Mun actively collects surplus dry and fresh food from a variety of donors, receiving both regular and ad-hoc contributions, including items nearing their shelf life and generous donations from partners.

Volunteers will conduct a thorough quality check and sorting process for these donations in the warehouse. They carefully record and evaluate how the food will be redistributed to partner charities and feeding programs that support at-risk elderly individuals, underprivileged children, and low-income families.

Volunteers will attend a short briefing in English at the start of the session and have a clear overview of the food bank and its operations.

	
Inventory checking, sorting food, labelling, packing items (eg. rice packing, mask packing etc), cleaning, and preparing for the food assistance programs. 



  



All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. If you wish to have a friend or family member join you on this activity, they must first register with Hands On and sign up for the activity.

occurrences.opportunityName: Re-think Plastic: Volunteer anytime anywhere to help solve excessive waste issue
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.



HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' recycling efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.



Remarks: Please note, you are not required to follow the stated dates and times listed in the calendar. This is for registration and recording purposes only.



Volunteer hours completed through this activity may not be recognized by all schools. Students should check with their school's coordinator.

occurrences.opportunityName: LeadOn: Empower women/elderly through expressive arts

occurrences.description:
This programme is generously supported by HKEX Charity Partnership Programme.



Description:

LeadOn Hong Kong is a volunteer leadership program  led by  HandsOn Hong Kong in partnership with HKEX Foundation. It is a structured leadership and community engagement program that guides and trains young people to build the skills to design and lead creative community projects.If you are interested in taking further steps by joining this program, please feel free to apply to the program here! 



We are recruiting volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at a number of expressive art workshops for the women/elderly served by our charity partners. These workshops use simple art-making activities to create a safe, welcoming space that enhances mood, confidence, and self-expression for participants.​ They help to improve well-being, reduce stress, and foster social connection for everyone involved. 



Volunteer Roles:




	
Set up and pack away art materials and any other preparation as needed. Support the Volunteer Leader and art therapist and/or facilitator by preparing simple art tools, distributing materials, and keeping the space tidy and safe.​

	
Encourage and accompany children with hearing impairments/elderly participants during activities, offering gentle guidance, conversation, and positive reinforcement.​

	
Assist with basic logistics such as registration, time-keeping, photos (where appropriate), and participant flow so the Volunteer Leader can focus on facilitation.​

	
Join a short briefing and debriefing led by the Volunteer Leader and/or HandsOn team to reflect on the impact of the session and share observations.​





Volunteers will support these service users on the following dates:



	
Nov 16: Ethnic minority elderly (English session)

	
Nov 18: Local elderly

	
Nov 22: Tai Po residents

	
Nov 30: Ethnic minority women (English session)

	
Dec 7: Ethnic minority elderly (English session)

	
Dec 17: Children & parents from new arrival families

	
Dec 23: Local elderly







Remarks:




	
This role does not involve designing or leading the workshop; you will be supporting trained Volunteer Leaders who have completed specialised expressive art and soft skills training under the LeadOn Hong Kong program.

	
The art workshops may cover soft pastels, chenille stems, art collage, plant printing, stone painting, and wood-slice painting.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

occurrences.opportunityName: Save bread for the less fortunate HK Island Wednesdays (Youth Welcome)
occurrences.managingOrganization: HKFoodWorks
occurrences.description:
Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Nan Dao Commercial Building, Sheung Wan from 8:30pm to 9:30pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
This programme is generously supported by HKEX Charity Partnership Programme.



 



Description:



LeadOn Hong Kong is a volunteer leadership program in Hong Kong led by young people roughly aged 18–35, run by the NGO HandsOn Hong Kong in partnership with HKEX Foundation. It is a structured leadership and community engagement program that guides and trains young people/adults to build the skills to design and lead creative community projects. serving local social needs.

 



Positioned as a bridge between young talent and the workforce, focusing on soft skills like communication, adaptability, and collaboration in a social-impact context. 

 



We are recruiting volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at board game-based service sessions for elderly people/young children at our partner NGO centres. These sessions use the power of play to create fun, structured opportunities for social interaction, cognitive stimulation, and skills-building in areas such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. These innovative board game workshops support social connection and cognitive engagement among elderly people and language development, creativity and confidence in children.





Children's Sessions (conduct in English through storytelling and board games):

Nov: 6, 7, 13, 14, 20, 21, 22, 27, 28

Dec: 4, 5, 11



Elderly Sessions:

Nov: 11, 17

Dec: 8, 9



Volunteer Roles:




	
Assist the Volunteer Leader and NGO staff in setting up the space, preparing game materials, and ensure all components are ready for use.

	
Join small groups to play board games with elderly participants/ children, modelling turn-taking, active listening, and inclusive participation.

	
​Support the Volunteer Leader in explaining simple game rules, encouraging quieter participants, and gently managing basic group dynamics during play.

	
Assist with smooth logistics such as registration, time-keeping, transition between games, and packing up at the end of the session.

	
​Participate in a briefing session and debriefing reflection to share what you observed about participants’ engagement and interactions.

	 





Remarks:




	
In this role, you will not be responsible for designing the program; you will be supporting trained Volunteer Leaders who have completed LeadOn’s Board Game Mastery and facilitation training to run impactful, participant-centred sessions.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

occurrences.opportunityName: Be an Event Volunteer at the Redress Secondhand Summer Pop-up Shop
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: 

Summer Pop-up Shop: The environmental charity Redress will be running a secondhand pop-up shop to resell a small portion of the unwanted clothes collected from the community to contribute to the circular economy in Hong Kong and reduce the amount of clothing waste going to landfill.  



What You Will Be Doing: 

1. In the back-of-house area: 

- Hanging, ironing and steaming clothes

- Organising clothes on different rails



2. On the shop floor:

- Replenishing and tidying up the shop floor 

- Welcoming customers and direct them to the different areas of the shop 





Remarks:

1. Volunteers must be at least 18 years of age

2. Please dress casually with closed-toe shoes and bring your own bottle of water

3. Please make sure to dress all black, easier to recognise your role

4. Redress staff may take photos to record the activity for the purpose of sharing and promoting the charity's work. Please inform a staff member on-site if you are uncomfortable with being photographed.

5. After their slot is completed, all volunteers benefit from a 10% discount at the pop-up shop (during opening hours)



Gathering location: 18/F Berkshire House , Taikoo Place, 25 Westlands Rd, Quarry Bay (香港鰂魚涌華蘭路25號太古坊栢克大廈18樓)



**Please note that we do not accept group or company volunteers for this activity

occurrences.description:
This programme is generously supported by HKEX Charity Partnership Programme.



 



Description:



In this session, we hope to train volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at board game-based service sessions for young children at our partner NGO centres. These sessions use the power of play to create fun, structured opportunities for social interaction, cognitive stimulation, and skills-building in areas such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. These innovative board game workshops support social connection, language development, creativity and confidence in children.



 





Your role as a workshop participant:

Volunteers will receive professional training in facilitating English board game activities, including selecting age-appropriate games, explaining rules clearly, and engaging children through interactive play. These transferable skills are essential for building rapport with children of different ages, while also creating a fun and supportive environment that enhances their language development, confidence, and social interaction through gameplay.



Opportunities after the workshop:

Upon completing the training, volunteers will have the opportunity to serve at community centres. This experience will allow you to apply your newly acquired skills in real settings while making a meaningful contribution to children’s learning and development. A follow-up email will be sent to volunteers after the information session to complete their registration for the service sessions.



 





Remarks:




	
Please sign up for any of the three sessions. The training contents are the same for the three sessions.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: LOVE 21 is a charity dedicated to bettering the lives of those living with Down syndrome and autism in Hong Kong through physical activity and nutrition. They run a variety of sports and exercise classes, art workshops, nutrition programs, and guardian counseling sessions.

Volunteer roles:




	
To be able to lead a subgroup independently.

	
To assist the tutor in teaching a group of 8-12 children or people aged 6-45 and with Down Syndrome and to be confident enough to practice with the students when the coach is working with other students.

	
To assist the tutor in helping the class run smoothly and safely, while also ensuring that everyone is actively engaged.

	
To motivate and energize participants throughout the class.







Language requirements for volunteers: Fluent in Cantonese (preferred but not required) 

All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. If you wish to have a friend or family member join you on this activity, they must first register with HandsOn and sign up for the activity.

occurrences.opportunityName: Collect Bread for Redistribution - Fortress Hill (Youth welcome)
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: In Hong Kong, 3,600 tonnes of food are discarded daily, while one in five people struggles to access nutritious meals. In response to this urgent need, Feeding Hong Kong's Bread Runs mobilise dedicated volunteers to collect surplus fresh bread and quality food from local stores near closing time. Volunteers play a crucial role in addressing hunger and reducing food waste in our community, helping us sustain this vital work.

These bread donations are redistributed the same night or first thing the following morning to local charities feeding people in need including shelters for the homeless, migrant workers, refugee support centres, children's homes and other non-profits supporting the vulnerable.    

Volunteers will work in teams of two to support Feeding Hong Kong’s Bread Run and collect food items from a store in  AIA Tower, Fortress Hill. And then deliver these items immediately to their Yau Tong warehouse.

occurrences.opportunityName: Deliver Necessities & Warmth to the Homeless Community in Happy Valley
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description:
On this Wanchai & Happy Valley Kindness Walk, you will see a wide range of individuals in great need and serve roughly 35 people experiencing homelessness. Apart from building connections with the homeless community, you will provide and distribute snacks and necessities to people in need.
 
ImpactHK’s aim for these walks is to build trust through kindness. As a charity they are on the streets at least once per day and their focus on building friendships is giving people a true second chance. In order to sustain housing and job creation initiatives by ImpactHK, we encourage each participant to donate $100 or more.

This walk starts from 12 Harbour Road, Wanchai, and takes around 1.5 hours to complete. Bring a reusable bag to carry the items to hand out.

Remarks: Volunteers between the ages of 10 and 14 must be accompanied by an adult to join this Kindness Walk. The guardian must first sign up for this activity. After successful registration, please email hohk@handsonhongkong.org to sign the child up. Volunteers between the ages of 15 and 18 who want to join the activity without an adult must obtain prior parental consent and email this to HandsOn Hong Kong in order to successfully register for the activity.

All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members must also register and sign up separately.
occurrences.locationCity: 12 Harbour Road, Wanchai
occurrences.locationZipCode: 香港香港島灣仔港灣道12號

occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港

occurrences.description:
This programme is generously supported by HKEX Charity Partnership Programme.



Description:

LeadOn Hong Kong is a volunteer leadership program  led by  HandsOn Hong Kong in partnership with HKEX Foundation. It is a structured leadership and community engagement program that guides and trains young people to build the skills to design and lead creative community projects.If you are interested in taking further steps by joining this program, please feel free to apply to the program here! 



We are recruiting volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at a number of expressive art workshops for the women/elderly served by our charity partners. These workshops use simple art-making activities to create a safe, welcoming space that enhances mood, confidence, and self-expression for participants.​ They help to improve well-being, reduce stress, and foster social connection for everyone involved. 



Volunteer Roles:




	
Set up and pack away art materials and any other preparation as needed. Support the Volunteer Leader and art therapist and/or facilitator by preparing simple art tools, distributing materials, and keeping the space tidy and safe.​

	
Encourage and accompany children with hearing impairments/elderly participants during activities, offering gentle guidance, conversation, and positive reinforcement.​

	
Assist with basic logistics such as registration, time-keeping, photos (where appropriate), and participant flow so the Volunteer Leader can focus on facilitation.​

	
Join a short briefing and debriefing led by the Volunteer Leader and/or HandsOn team to reflect on the impact of the session and share observations.​





Volunteers will support these service users on the following dates:



	
Nov 16: Ethnic minority elderly (English session)

	
Nov 18: Local elderly

	
Nov 22: Tai Po residents

	
Nov 30: Ethnic minority women (English session)

	
Dec 7: Ethnic minority elderly (English session)

	
Dec 17: Children & parents from new arrival families

	
Dec 23: Local elderly







Remarks:




	
This role does not involve designing or leading the workshop; you will be supporting trained Volunteer Leaders who have completed specialised expressive art and soft skills training under the LeadOn Hong Kong program.

	
The art workshops may cover soft pastels, chenille stems, art collage, plant printing, stone painting, and wood-slice painting.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Causeway Bay Windsor House (皇室堡)(Entrance near the parking on Great George Street) from 8:45pm to 10:00pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.opportunityName: Phone call support to 1 elderly individual [PRE-TRAINED VOLUNTEERS ONLY]
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Each volunteer joining this support-program must have attended our information session before and be available to support ONE elderly individual, by making one phone call each week over a four-week period.
 
First phone calls will be made on Saturday Oct 1st—after then a suitable day and time for calling will be determined between the volunteer and the elderly person they are supporting. Once you signed up for the June 18th session, it means that you're available for the four-week period and our staff will help you sign up for the remaining three sessions (this is important for our tracking purposes).

Description: Many elderly residents in Hong Kong struggle with social isolation, as they become disconnected from their families and communities. Without regular visitors or conversation, the effects of loneliness can be severe for this vulnerable population, including increased risk of anxiety, depression, and cognitive decline. Help from the city's volunteers is needed to provide companionship and support for Hong Kong's isolated elderly residents.


Volunteer roles: Each volunteer will be assigned one elderly individual to call on the phone and check in with once a week. They will provide social connection and emotional support and help their district’s elderly centre to determine their well-being and immediate needs.

All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong.

occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.

By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.

occurrences.opportunityName: Re-think Plastic: Volunteer anytime anywhere to help solve excessive waste issue
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.



HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' recycling efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.



Remarks: Please note, you are not required to follow the stated dates and times listed in the calendar. This is for registration and recording purposes only.

occurrences.description:
Description: 

Summer Pop-up Shop: The environmental charity Redress will be running a secondhand pop-up shop to resell a small portion of the unwanted clothes collected from the community to contribute to the circular economy in Hong Kong and reduce the amount of clothing waste going to landfill.  



What You Will Be Doing: 

1. In the back-of-house area: 

- Hanging, ironing and steaming clothes

- Organising clothes on different rails



2. On the shop floor:

- Welcoming customers and direct them to the different areas of the shop

Volunteer Roles:

1. HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' exercising efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below, you are committing to exercise anytime and anywhere from Tuesday, 6 pm to Thursday, 6 pm.

occurrences.opportunityName: Help at animal shelter in Yuen Long (Youth Welcome)
occurrences.organizationServedName: Maison De Charlotte Pour Des Chats Et Des Chiens Sarl Limited (MCCC) 沙律貓狗之家
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Maison De Charlotte Pour Des Chats Et Des Chiens Sarl Limited (MCCC) is a small non-profit organization founded in 1997 and takes in about 200 animals. With no funding and limited manpower and resources, MCCC has been working hard for many years to provide a warm home to the countless rescued cats and dogs and let those waiting to be adopted live happily and have enough space for running and jumping. The founder’s mission is to "influence life with life" and fight for the right to survive for abandoned animals and provide them with the most appropriate medical treatment. They never make a hasty decision to end the life of an animal, nor delay or stingy medical expenses. They hope to disseminate information about respect for life, love for animals, "adopt, don’t abandon" and so on.

Volunteer roles:





	
Wash the water pockets for dogs and refill water

	
Clean up the dog's poo

	
Clean up areas where the dogs sleep, including blankets and towels

	
Assist in feeding the dogs, preparing meals, cleaning and washing dishes afterward

	
Have great fun with the dogs! 





Remarks:



	
Volunteers must be 16 years old or over. Parental consent is needed for volunteers age 16-17 years old. Please send an email to hohk@handsonhongkong.org with your parental consent to confirm your slots. 

	
Please note that this is an outdoor animal shelter without air-conditioners.






	
Volunteers are suggested to bring: 

	

		
At least 1-liter water & food 

		
​Sunscreen

		
Towels and an extra set of clothing for changing in case you get dirty.

		
A pair of slippers/rainboots for cleaning the kennel   

	

	



All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.



For the record proof, after the volunteer has completed the service, you can log in to your account and click on Volunteer> My account> Overview, and click the 'Print Volunteer History' at the bottom of the page to save the volunteer record which can be served as the official proof document.

occurrences.description:
Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Nan Dao Commercial Building, Sheung Wan from 8:30pm to 9:30pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.

Description: Paws United Charity (PUC) is a non-profit, all-volunteer rescue organization established and registered in Hong Kong (ORG00102).

 

A group of animal-loving volunteers who are passionate about animal rescue and have worked together across various rescue projects in Hong Kong. After many years of hard work and dedication, they finally have a ‘home’ to call their own.

Important Note: Please be aware that some dogs, particularly puppies, are very energetic and at times, boisterous. DO NOT wear clothes that are too loose or overly-exposed

		
NO swimwear, swim trunks, sandals, or slippers. 

	

	

	
Meals:
	

		
Please have your meal before coming as there is no meal break. We understand that the duty may be energy-consuming, but you are welcome to bring snacks/bread or small bites for a short snack break in centre.

occurrences.opportunityName: Help out with a cigarette butt cleanup in Tseung Kwan O(for volunteer aged 5-15)
occurrences.organizationServedName: Plastic Free Seas 無塑海洋
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Plastic Free Seas,  大便妹，學環保 and Here in Nature have partnered to organise a cigarette butt cleanup in support of global No Butts Day. This action aims to raise awareness of cigarette butt pollution and gather data to encourage legislation banning disposable cigarette butts.



A volunteer leader will meet you at the start of the event, provide a safety and instruction brief, and a debrief at the end of the cleanup.



This event is for children between the ages of 5 and 15. One child can be signed up for each adult that has been registered on the adult's event page. Do NOT sign up a child until you have successfully registered an adult. Children aged 16+ to sign up on the adult's event page.



Time: 4 pm - 5 pm



Meeting point: Tseung Kwan O MTR Station Exit A2



What you will do: Collect used cigarette butts you find on the ground, and count them at the end of the event

* Gloves and BBQ-style tongs will be provided

* Wear comfortable shoes and clothing, a hat, bring a full reusable water bottle and sun protection

* Bring a backpack that is easy to carry your belongings in while picking up cigarette butts

* Bring a small bag or container to collect cigarette butts in



Remarks:

* Please do not bring single-use items to this event, such as disposable plastic bottles, disposable raincoats, etc.

occurrences.description:
Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Causeway Bay Windsor House (皇室堡)(Entrance near the parking on Great George Street) from 8:45pm to 10:00pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.opportunityName: Phone call support to 1 elderly individual [PRE-TRAINED VOLUNTEERS ONLY]
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Each volunteer joining this support-program must have attended our information session before and be available to support ONE elderly individual, by making one phone call each week over a four-week period.
 
First phone calls will be made on Saturday Oct 1st—after then a suitable day and time for calling will be determined between the volunteer and the elderly person they are supporting. Once you signed up for the June 18th session, it means that you're available for the four-week period and our staff will help you sign up for the remaining three sessions (this is important for our tracking purposes).

Description: Many elderly residents in Hong Kong struggle with social isolation, as they become disconnected from their families and communities. Without regular visitors or conversation, the effects of loneliness can be severe for this vulnerable population, including increased risk of anxiety, depression, and cognitive decline. Help from the city's volunteers is needed to provide companionship and support for Hong Kong's isolated elderly residents.


Volunteer roles: Each volunteer will be assigned one elderly individual to call on the phone and check in with once a week. They will provide social connection and emotional support and help their district’s elderly centre to determine their well-being and immediate needs.

All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. 

每個參加此計劃的義工都必須已出席我們之前舉行的簡介會，並且能在四週的時間內每週致電一位長者一次。

義工將在10月1日（星期六）首次致電長者，然後義工和他們所負責的長者之間確定合適的通話日期和時間。當你報名參與此計劃，即表示你能在四週的時間內每週致電一位長者一次，牽手香港員工會協助你註冊餘下3節服務（牽手香港員工將利用這四節服務追蹤義工的服務時數）。

活動簡介：因應疫情影響，香港大部分長者都擔心或無法外出，唯有留在家中自我隔離以保障健康，因此這些弱勢群體迫切需要義工的幫助，來支援他們的心理健康。社會隔離的影響可能包括焦慮，沮喪甚至認知能力下降。

義工角色：每位義工將獲分配一名長者的聯絡方式，義工需每週致電一次，提供社交聯繫和情感支持，並幫助中心了解他們的健康和迫切需要。

occurrences.opportunityName: Help empower Hongkongers to recycle their glass
occurrences.managingOrganization: Greeners South 南地球
occurrences.description:
Description: Green Glass Green is an initiative started by truck drivers in Hong Kong who witnessed first-hand the vast amount of glass being wasted and dumped at landfills. Since launching their conservation efforts in 2010, they have been helping to promote greener living in Hong Kong by empowering people to reduce and reuse as well as actively collecting glass bottles for recycling.



Volunteer roles:

Volunteers will help the Green Glass Green team run a glass recycling awareness booth to encourage residents of the Lei Tung Estate to recycle their glass items. Help is needed with setting up the booth, assisting with actual glass collection and addressing questions from residents.

 



Volunteer's feedback and reflection:

After participating in the recycling glass service, I learned a lot about recycling and am motivated to do more in my daily life. The response from the community was overwhelmingly positive, and many people were eager to learn more about sustainable recycling practices. This project was a rewarding experience that taught me the value of community service and the power of education in creating positive change. It exceeded my expectations, as I had assumed that most people would find recycling to be an inconvenient task. However, I was pleasantly surprised to see so many people interested in learning about the benefits of recycling. 



All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately. If you have any questions, please email us at hohk@handsonhongkong.org

occurrences.opportunityName: Organize a drive to raise food items for the Community Fridges
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Frontline charities are seeing a significant increase in the number of people needing food assistance which they expect to last well beyond this year. Gift n Take, one of the local nonprofits, leaving stocked-up and unplugged “Community Fridges” with food in the community for people in need to take for free. Those community fridges are now calling for volunteers' support by filling with food. Families and individuals can support this project by rallying their community to raise food items for those community fridges.  This non-profit has a specific list of items they need, listed below. By signing up to support one of these you commit to raising all their required items and delivering them directly to the charity—with the help of friends, neighbours or colleagues!



Please collect the suggested below items: 

 


	
Canned food 

	
Instant noodles/Dried noodles 

	
Biscuits 

	
Rice 





Volunteer roles:


 




	
Before signing up to raise the items needed below give consideration to whether you can rally your community to help you raise the items needed—we’ve seen many families, individuals and families do this successfully! Volunteers typically use their homes for storage until all items have been gathered

	
You will need to deliver your items directly to the community fridge within a week after receiving our service reminder (coming from HOHK@handsonhongkong.org). 

	
Please take a photo after putting those donated items in the fridge, and send this photo back to HOHK@handsonhongkong.org.

occurrences.opportunityName: Re-think Plastic: Volunteer anytime anywhere to help solve excessive waste issue
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.



HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' recycling efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.



Remarks: Please note, you are not required to follow the stated dates and times listed in the calendar. This is for registration and recording purposes only.



Volunteer hours completed through this activity may not be recognized by all schools. Students should check with their school's coordinator.

Description: “FOODSPORT WEDNESDAY” is the weekly recurring calorie drive, taking place virtually so all can participate, regardless of location. 2. Click here: https://www.foodsport.com.hk/fswednesday to follow the Submission Record Method procedures to submit your calorie-burnt record to FoodSport.



3. Within 14 days of your registered session, send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.

occurrences.description:
Description: LOVE 21 is a charity dedicated to bettering the lives of those living with Down syndrome and autism in Hong Kong through physical activity and nutrition. They run a variety of sports and exercise classes, art workshops, nutrition programs, and guardian counseling sessions.

Volunteer roles:




	
To be able to lead a subgroup independently.

	
To assist the tutor in teaching a group of 8-12 children or people aged 6-45 and with Down Syndrome and to be confident enough to practice with the students when the coach is working with other students.

	
To assist the tutot in helping the class run smoothly and safely, while also ensuring that everyone is actively engaged.

	
To motivate and energize participants throughout the class.







Language requirements for volunteers: Fluent in Cantonese (preferred but not required) 

All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. If you wish to have a friend or family member join you on this activity, they must first register with HandsOn and sign up for the activity.

occurrences.opportunityName: Save bread for the less fortunate HK Island Mondays (Youth Welcome)
occurrences.managingOrganization: HKFoodWorks
occurrences.description:
Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Nan Dao Commercial Building, Sheung Wan from 8:30pm to 9:30pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.
occurrences.locationCity: Kowloon & Hong Kong Island
occurrences.locationZipCode: 九龍及香港島

occurrences.opportunityName: Deliver Necessities and Warmth to Homeless Community in Yau Ma Tei
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description:On this Yau Ma Tei Kindness Walk, you will see a wide range of individuals in great need and serve roughly 35 people experiencing homelessness. Apart from building connections with the homeless community, you will provide and distribute snacks and necessities to people in need.
 
ImpactHK’s aim for these walks is to build trust through kindness. As a charity, they are on the streets at least once per day and their focus on building friendships in the hope of creating opportunities for change. In order to sustain housing and job creation initiatives by ImpactHK, we encourage each participant to donate $100 or more.
 
This walk gathers at a shop in Jordan and takes 2 hours to complete. Bring a reusable bag to carry the items to hand out.
 
Parental guidance is required for volunteers under the age of 16. We do not suggest this walk for children under 10.  
 
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members must also register and sign up separately.

 
Remarks: Volunteers between the ages of 10 and 14 must be accompanied by an adult to join this Kindness Walk. The guardian must first sign up for this activity. After successful registration, please email hohk@handsonhongkong.org to sign the child up. Volunteers between the ages of 15 and 18 who want to join the activity without an adult must obtain prior parental consent and email this to HandsOn Hong Kong in order to successfully register for the activity.
occurrences.locationCity: 51 Pitt Street, Mong Kok

occurrences.opportunityName: Small Group Workshop Facilitator (7 July)
occurrences.managingOrganization: Kids4Kids 童協基金會
occurrences.description:
Kids4Kids envisions a future where all young people are empowered to be changemakers with the belief that they are never too young to change the world.We are looking for energetic volunteers to help out in Power Your Future workshops (PYF)! You will help to support low-resource secondary school students to participate in hands-on activities and facilitate small group discussions. Power Your Future enables youth to explore their strengths and bring out their best. Interactive activities develop confidence and emotional intelligence, preparing them for solving community issues together in Hong Kong.




	
Volunteers must attend an in-person training a week before the first workshop

	
Volunteers must inform the organization if they are unable to attend the workshops

	
Please arrive at the venue 15 min prior to the specified time

	
While it is preferred that volunteers attend all scheduled dates, those who cannot will be provided with a form to indicate which dates they can attend

	
Assist 80-130 students in small groups to participate in activities.

	
Facilitate group discussions in small groups

	
Ensure that everyone feels comfortable participating and expressing their ideas

	
LANGUAGE requirement: Cantonese, Mandarin (Optional)
occurrences.locationCity: Sha Tin Government Secondary School, 11 Man Lai Road, Shatin

occurrences.opportunityName: Help and Deliver Your Care at Paws United Charity Dog Adoption Centre
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Paws United Charity (PUC) is a non-profit, all-volunteer rescue organization established and registered in Hong Kong (ORG00102).

 

A group of animal-loving volunteers who are passionate about animal rescue and have worked together across various rescue projects in Hong Kong. After many years of hard work and dedication, they finally have a ‘home’ to call their own.



Volunteer roles:

1. Taking care and socializing with puppies

2. Cleansing

3. Assisting visitors by introducing Paws United Charity and the puppies to them



This will serve PUC’s core mission to continue to improve the lives of animals in our community by promoting responsible pet ownership, humane treatment of animals, and choosing adoption instead of purchase. 



Important Note: Please be aware that some dogs, particularly puppies, are very energetic and at times, boisterous. Volunteers should be comfortable handling dogs with this level of energy and enthusiasm, and we recommend wearing appropriate clothing (as detailed below) to minimise nips or scratches. 



Remarks:


	
Only successfully registered volunteers for this activity are allowed to join this activity. Please DO NOT bring any unregistered volunteers, your kids, or pets to volunteer.

	
Clothing: 
	

		
Wear something comfortable and things you don’t mind getting dirty in.

		
DO NOT wear clothes that are too loose or overly-exposed

		
NO swimwear, swim trunks, sandals, or slippers. 

	

	

	
Meals:
	

		
Please have your meal before coming as there is no meal break. We understand that the duty may be energy-consuming, but you are welcome to bring snacks/bread or small bites for a short snack break in centre.
occurrences.locationCity: The Pulse, Repulse Bay
occurrences.locationZipCode: 淺水灣

occurrences.opportunityName: Packing & sorting food in Tuen Mun for Hong Kong's most vulnerable
occurrences.organizationServedName: Youth With A Mission Tuen Mun Hong Kong
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description:  Job losses and financial hardships have led to a notable rise in families seeking assistance from charities for essential food needs. YWAM Tuen Mun actively collects surplus dry and fresh food from a variety of donors, receiving both regular and ad-hoc contributions, including items nearing their shelf life and generous donations from partners.

Volunteers will conduct a thorough quality check and sorting process for these donations in the warehouse. They carefully record and evaluate how the food will be redistributed to partner charities and feeding programs that support at-risk elderly individuals, underprivileged children, and low-income families.




Volunteer roles:



	
Volunteers will attend a short briefing in English at the start of the session and have a clear overview of the food bank and its operations.

	
Inventory checking, sorting food, labelling, packing items (eg. rice packing, mask packing etc), cleaning, and preparing for the food assistance programs. 



  



All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. If you wish to have a friend or family member join you on this activity, they must first register with Hands On and sign up for the activity.

occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: In Hong Kong, 3,600 tonnes of food are discarded daily, while one in five people struggles to access nutritious meals. In response to this urgent need, Feeding Hong Kong's Bread Runs mobilise dedicated volunteers to collect surplus fresh bread and quality food from local stores near closing time. Volunteers play a crucial role in addressing hunger and reducing food waste in our community, helping us sustain this vital work.

These bread donations are redistributed the same night or first thing the following morning to local charities feeding people in need including shelters for the homeless, migrant workers, refugee support centres, children's homes and other non-profits supporting the vulnerable.    

Volunteers will work in teams of two to support Feeding Hong Kong’s Bread Run and collect food items from a store in  AIA Tower, Fortress Hill. And then deliver these items immediately to their Yau Tong warehouse.

Description:  Job losses and financial hardships have led to a notable rise in families seeking assistance from charities for essential food needs. YWAM Tuen Mun actively collects surplus dry and fresh food from a variety of donors, receiving both regular and ad-hoc contributions, including items nearing their shelf life and generous donations from partners.

occurrences.opportunityName: Re-think Plastic: Volunteer anytime anywhere to help solve excessive waste issue
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.



HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' recycling efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.



Remarks: Please note, you are not required to follow the stated dates and times listed in the calendar. This is for registration and recording purposes only.



Volunteer hours completed through this activity may not be recognized by all schools. Students should check with their school's coordinator.

Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Nan Dao Commercial Building, Sheung Wan from 8:30pm to 9:30pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.opportunityName: LeadOn: Help to facilitate a boardgame workshop that uplifts children/elderly
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
This programme is generously supported by HKEX Charity Partnership Programme.



 



Description:



LeadOn Hong Kong is a volunteer leadership program in Hong Kong led by young people roughly aged 18–35, run by the NGO HandsOn Hong Kong in partnership with HKEX Foundation. It is a structured leadership and community engagement program that guides and trains young people/adults to build the skills to design and lead creative community projects. serving local social needs.

 



Positioned as a bridge between young talent and the workforce, focusing on soft skills like communication, adaptability, and collaboration in a social-impact context. 

 



We are recruiting volunteers to get hands-on with our LeadOn Volunteer Leaders at board game-based service sessions for elderly people/young children at our partner NGO centres. These sessions use the power of play to create fun, structured opportunities for social interaction, cognitive stimulation, and skills-building in areas such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. These innovative board game workshops support social connection and cognitive engagement among elderly people and language development, creativity and confidence in children.



 



Volunteer Roles:




	
Assist the Volunteer Leader and NGO staff in setting up the space, preparing game materials, and ensure all components are ready for use.

	
Join small groups to play board games with elderly participants/ children, modelling turn-taking, active listening, and inclusive participation.

	
​Support the Volunteer Leader in explaining simple game rules, encouraging quieter participants, and gently managing basic group dynamics during play.

	
Assist with smooth logistics such as registration, time-keeping, transition between games, and packing up at the end of the session.

	
​Participate in a briefing session and debriefing reflection to share what you observed about participants’ engagement and interactions.

	 





Remarks:




	
In this role, you will not be responsible for designing the program; you will be supporting trained Volunteer Leaders who have completed LeadOn’s Board Game Mastery and facilitation training to run impactful, participant-centred sessions.

	
All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members who wish to join are warmly welcome—please ensure that each person registers and signs up separately.

To be comfortable with playing trampoline.

occurrences.description:
Description:
On this Wanchai & Happy Valley Kindness Walk, you will see a wide range of individuals in great need and serve roughly 35 people experiencing homelessness. Apart from building connections with the homeless community, you will provide and distribute snacks and necessities to people in need.
 
ImpactHK’s aim for these walks is to build trust through kindness. As a charity they are on the streets at least once per day and their focus on building friendships is giving people a true second chance. In order to sustain housing and job creation initiatives by ImpactHK, we encourage each participant to donate $100 or more.

This walk starts from 12 Harbour Road, Wanchai, and takes around 1.5 hours to complete. Bring a reusable bag to carry the items to hand out.

Remarks: Volunteers between the ages of 10 and 14 must be accompanied by an adult to join this Kindness Walk. The guardian must first sign up for this activity. After successful registration, please email hohk@handsonhongkong.org to sign the child up. Volunteers between the ages of 15 and 18 who want to join the activity without an adult must obtain prior parental consent and email this to HandsOn Hong Kong in order to successfully register for the activity.

All volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members must also register and sign up separately.

occurrences.opportunityName: Help and Deliver Your Care at Paws United Charity Dog Adoption Centre
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Paws United Charity (PUC) is a non-profit, all-volunteer rescue organization established and registered in Hong Kong (ORG00102).

 

A group of animal-loving volunteers who are passionate about animal rescue and have worked together across various rescue projects in Hong Kong. After many years of hard work and dedication, they finally have a ‘home’ to call their own.



Volunteer roles:

1. Taking care and socializing with puppies

2. Cleansing

3. Assisting visitors by introducing Paws United Charity and the puppies to them



This will serve PUC’s core mission to continue to improve the lives of animals in our community by promoting responsible pet ownership, humane treatment of animals, and choosing adoption instead of purchase. 



Important Note: Please be aware that some dogs, particularly puppies, are very energetic and at times, boisterous. Volunteers should be comfortable handling dogs with this level of energy and enthusiasm, and we recommend wearing appropriate clothing (as detailed below) to minimise nips or scratches. 



Remarks:


	
Only successfully registered volunteers for this activity are allowed to join this activity. Please DO NOT bring any unregistered volunteers, your kids, or pets to volunteer.

	
Clothing: 
	

		
Wear something comfortable and things you don’t mind getting dirty in.

		
DO NOT wear clothes that are too loose or overly-exposed

		
NO swimwear, swim trunks, sandals, or slippers. 

	

	

	
Meals:
	

		
Please have your meal before coming as there is no meal break. We understand that the duty may be energy-consuming, but you are welcome to bring snacks/bread or small bites for a short snack break in centre.

occurrences.opportunityName: Assemble hygiene kits for the Toiletries Project
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description:

The Amber Foundation invites you to support their “The Toiletries Project”, a key initiative dedicated to providing essential hygiene items to vulnerable and less resourced communities across Hong Kong.



Access to basic toiletries is fundamental to health, yet it remains a challenge for many. This project fills that gap by collecting, assembling, and distributing vital hygiene kits to those in looking for support, including women in shelters, domestic workers, individuals living on the streets, elderly, and refugee communities. The foundation utilises donated items, such as airline amenity kits and hotel toiletries, to maximize resources and minimize waste.



By volunteering, you’ll play a direct role in fostering health, dignity, and a sense of care for our beneficiaries. Your participation also helps create a fun environment on the day!  



Volunteer Roles


	
Sorting and Categorising: Unpack and categorise a variety of incoming donated items, including individual and bulk toiletries, as well as specific items like airline kits.

	
Assemble the donation hygiene kits according to a specified checklist.





Remarks:

-Volunteers aged 12 to 15 must be accompanied by a legal guardian (for individual sign-ups) or an adult supervisor (for group registrations). To register a minor, the guardian must first sign up for the activity themselves; once registered, please email hohk@handsonhongkong.org to sign the child up for the session (Please ensure there is still an available spot for the child before emailing us.).

-Volunteers must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. Friends or family members must also register and sign up separately.

occurrences.description:
Description: Everyday in Hong Kong, over 3,250 tonnes of food waste are dumped into landfills, while one in five people live in poverty and struggle to eat.





Breadline is Hong Kong’s first public digital platform for food rescue. Volunteers connect with bakeries on Breadline to rescue leftover bread using real-time updates to make every run count.





Together, we save resources from being wasted and we support the homeless; low-income families; refugees and their children and the elderly poor, by delivering bread the same night to our grassroots partners.



 Important first step: To participate, you must sign up on the Breadline platform and secure your chosen bakeries ahead of time. Bakery slots are highly competitive and operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis—they go fast, so book your run early!





Volunteer Role:



Save bread!



- Choose your own runs on Breadline by selecting the bakeries you want to collect from



- Check-in for real-time updates and bring your own bags to collect



- Be agile and flexible, go to where the bread is!





Service time: Pick-up time is the one stated for your shop. You can drop-off your collection in Causeway Bay Windsor House (皇室堡)(Entrance near the parking on Great George Street) from 8:45pm to 10:00pm. Volunteers will be there to welcome you with your haul.



If you sign up as a team, each teammate should claim their own runs. 





Service details and volunteer safety: All volunteers will receive a service reminder for this activity which must be followed exactly to ensure timely bread collection and handling guidelines are followed.

occurrences.opportunityName: Phone call support to 1 elderly individual [PRE-TRAINED VOLUNTEERS ONLY]
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Each volunteer joining this support-program must have attended our information session before and be available to support ONE elderly individual, by making one phone call each week over a four-week period.
 
First phone calls will be made on Saturday Oct 1st—after then a suitable day and time for calling will be determined between the volunteer and the elderly person they are supporting. Once you signed up for the June 18th session, it means that you're available for the four-week period and our staff will help you sign up for the remaining three sessions (this is important for our tracking purposes).

Description: Many elderly residents in Hong Kong struggle with social isolation, as they become disconnected from their families and communities. Without regular visitors or conversation, the effects of loneliness can be severe for this vulnerable population, including increased risk of anxiety, depression, and cognitive decline. Help from the city's volunteers is needed to provide companionship and support for Hong Kong's isolated elderly residents.


Volunteer roles: Each volunteer will be assigned one elderly individual to call on the phone and check in with once a week. They will provide social connection and emotional support and help their district’s elderly centre to determine their well-being and immediate needs.

All volunteers who attend this activity must be registered with HandsOn Hong Kong. 

每個參加此計劃的義工都必須已出席我們之前舉行的簡介會，並且能在四週的時間內每週致電一位長者一次。

義工將在10月1日（星期六）首次致電長者，然後義工和他們所負責的長者之間確定合適的通話日期和時間。當你報名參與此計劃，即表示你能在四週的時間內每週致電一位長者一次，牽手香港員工會協助你註冊餘下3節服務（牽手香港員工將利用這四節服務追蹤義工的服務時數）。

活動簡介：因應疫情影響，香港大部分長者都擔心或無法外出，唯有留在家中自我隔離以保障健康，因此這些弱勢群體迫切需要義工的幫助，來支援他們的心理健康。社會隔離的影響可能包括焦慮，沮喪甚至認知能力下降。

occurrences.opportunityName: Re-think Plastic: Volunteer anytime anywhere to help solve excessive waste issue
occurrences.organizationServedName: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.managingOrganization: HandsOn Hong Kong 牽手香港
occurrences.description:
Description: Calls to reduce, reuse and recycle in Hong Kong have never been stronger. At the start of 2022, it was estimated that over 100 million pieces of plastic items had been used and disposed of by hotel quarantine guests alone. It has been predicted that by 2030, Hong Kong will be sending 4.2 billion single-use takeaway containers to landfill every year.



For Hongkongers looking to recycle in your own district, check out the GREEN @ COMMUNITY stores across the city, run by the Environmental Protection Department.  A full list of locations and addresses can be found here.



The separation and cleaning of items is a must and made easy on-site. Eight types of recyclables are accepted including paper, metals, plastics, glass bottles, certain electrical equipment, rechargeable batteries and more.



HandsOn would like to celebrate our volunteers' recycling efforts by recognizing your time and commitment with volunteer hours! By signing up for one of the dates below you are committing to drop off your recyclables within 14 days of your registered session and send a photo to HandsOn. We will reward the volunteer hours to your account accordingly.



Remarks: Please note, you are not required to follow the stated dates and times listed in the calendar. This is for registration and recording purposes only.



Volunteer hours completed through this activity may not be recognized by all schools. Students should check with their school's coordinator.

Description: On this Yau Ma Tei Kindness Walk, you will see a wide range of individuals in great need and serve roughly 50 homeless individuals. Apart from building connections with the homeless community, you will provide and distribute necessities including food and drinks to the people in need.

ImpactHK’s aim for these walks is to build trust through kindness. As a charity, they are on the streets at least once per day and their focus on building friendships in the hope of creating opportunities for change. This walk starts from ImpactHK's Guest Room, and takes nearly 1.5 hours to complete. Please bring a reusable bag to carry the items to hand out. 


This is a family friendly Kindness Walk.  Parental guidance is required for volunteers under the age of 15. 

Volunteers between the ages of 6 and 14 must be accompanied by an adult to join this Kindness Walk. The guardian must first sign up for this activity. After successful registration, please email hohk@handsonhongkong.org to sign the child up. Volunteers between the ages of 15 and 18 who want to join the activity without an adult must obtain prior parental consent and email this to HandsOn Hong Kong in order to successfully register for the activity.
